**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination — Hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914)**
- **Member:** Reese Grant
- **Member ID:** W386277495
- **Reference number:** POC-AC94C7BBDE-82539
- **Date of denial notice:** August 1, 2026
- **Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0736 — Hip Preservation Surgery (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0736.html)

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing Aetna's denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), issued on August 1, 2026 under reference number POC-AC94C7BBDE-82539. The notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision. Below I set out the plan's own criteria from Aetna CPB 0736 — Hip Preservation Surgery and point to the specific records in my chart that correspond to each one. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

If any particular record is still missing from the file, I am glad to supply it. I would ask that Aetna identify in writing exactly which document or criterion it found lacking, so that the gap can be closed rather than guessed at.

---

## The plan's criteria and what my records show

**1. Imaging diagnosis of definite FAI with labral pathology**

The policy states:

> "Diagnosis of definite femoro-acetabular impingement (FAI) defined by appropriate imaging studies (X-rays, MRI or CT scans), showing labral pathology (e.g. partial or full thickness labral tearing or labral damage) with one or more of the following:"

My MRI arthrogram of the hip, dated June 15, 2026, reports an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement. That is a labral tear identified on an appropriate imaging study, which is what this criterion asks for.

The policy then lists imaging findings, one or more of which must be present, including:

> "cam impingement (alpha angle greater than 50 degrees)"

My MRI arthrogram reports an alpha angle of **68 degrees**, and expressly describes cam-type impingement. Sixty-eight degrees is above the threshold the plan itself has published. The policy also lists pincer impingement ("pincer impingement (acetabular retroversion or coxa profunda) (center edge angle greater than or equal to 40 degrees), or") and "pistol grip deformity (non-spherical femoral head shape); and" as alternatives; only one is required, and the cam criterion is met.

The policy further provides:

> "For purposes of this policy, Aetna will consider the official written report of complex imaging studies (e.g., CT, MRI, myelogram). If the operating surgeon disagrees with the official written report, the surgeon should document that disagreement."

The findings above are taken from the official written report of the MRI arthrogram. There is no disagreement between my surgeon and that report to document. If the report itself is not in the file, I ask that Aetna tell me so and I will have it sent again.

**2. Moderate to severe symptoms typical of FAI, of at least six months' duration**

The policy states:

> "Moderate to severe symptoms typical of FAI (hip or groin pain that is worsened by flexion activities (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) that significantly limits activities, with duration of at least 6 months where diagnosis of FAI has been made as above; and"

My records document 18 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest. I have sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and with pivoting, and I cannot run or squat. That is groin pain worsened by flexion activities — prolonged sitting and squatting are the two examples the policy itself gives — and it significantly limits what I can do. Eighteen months is three times the six-month duration the plan requires.

**3. Positive impingement sign**

The policy states:

> "Positive impingement sign with sudden pain on 90 degree hip flexion with adduction and internal rotation or extension and external rotation; and"

My examination records document positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. If Aetna requires the examining physician's description of the specific maneuver and result in the exact terms used in the policy, that is a documentation item my surgeon's office can provide on request, and I ask that it be identified as such rather than treated as an absence of clinical findings.

**4. Failure of conservative treatment**

The policy states:

> "Failure to respond to all available conservative treatment options including: activity modification (e.g., restriction of athletic pursuits and avoidance of symptomatic motion), pharmacological intervention (e.g., non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDS]), injections of local anesthetics into the joint) and physiotherapy."

Each category listed is documented in my chart:

- *Activity modification* — included in my supervised physical therapy program and documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- *Pharmacological intervention* — NSAIDs taken for four months, with inadequate relief.
- *Injection into the joint* — a corticosteroid injection on April 11, 2026, which gave only two weeks of partial relief.
- *Physiotherapy* — supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization, from April 20, 2026 to June 29, 2026, with 18 visits completed.

None of it resolved my symptoms, which is why my surgeon has recommended surgery.

The policy adds a duration requirement:

> "The treatment should be for at least 12 weeks in the past year with at least 6 weeks being formal physiotherapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist not virtual)."

My conservative treatment in the past year runs well beyond 12 weeks: four months of NSAIDs, a joint injection on April 11, 2026, and supervised physical therapy with activity modification from April 20, 2026 through June 29, 2026. Within that course, the formal physiotherapy component was 10 weeks and 18 visits of supervised, in-person physical therapy — more than the 6 weeks of formal physiotherapy the policy specifies. I want to be straightforward with Aetna that the physical therapy episode itself spanned 10 weeks; read as the policy is written, the 12-week requirement applies to the overall course of conservative treatment and the 6-week requirement to the formal physiotherapy inside it, and my records satisfy both.

The policy also states:

> "Physical therapy (PT) needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history; and"

My physical therapy is documented in the physical therapy discharge note, and the 18 visits between April 20 and June 29, 2026 should also appear in Aetna's own claims history for me. Both confirmation routes the policy allows are available. My treating physical therapist was [PT provider/clinic name — to be completed], and I can have the full notes resent if they are not in the file.

**5. No advanced arthritis, and no joint space narrowing**

The policy states:

> "Absence of advanced osteoarthritis change on pre-operative X-ray (Tonnis grade 2 or more) or severe cartilage injury (Outerbridge grade III or IV); and"

and:

> "Absence of joint space narrowing on plain radiograph of the pelvis. Joint space is not less than 2 mm wide anywhere along the sourcil; and"

My June 15, 2026 imaging reports **Tonnis grade 0** and **preserved joint space**. Tonnis grade 0 is below the grade 2 threshold the policy sets, and preserved joint space is the finding these criteria are looking for. If Aetna requires a pre-operative plain radiograph report with a sourcil measurement stated in millimetres, or an Outerbridge grading, I ask that this be named specifically so my surgeon's office can address it.

**6. Laxity disorders, osteogenesis imperfecta, and other sources of pain**

The policy states:

> "Member does not have generalized joint laxity especially in diseases connected with hypermobility of the joints, such as Marfan syndrome and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome; and"

> "Member does not have osteogenesis imperfecta; and"

> "All other potential sources of hip pain have been ruled out."

My submitted records contain no diagnosis of generalized joint laxity, Marfan syndrome, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, or osteogenesis imperfecta. My records also show no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoking status. My surgeon's evaluation, together with the MRI arthrogram, is the basis for the FAI diagnosis; if Aetna requires a separate written statement that other sources of hip pain have been excluded, my surgeon can provide it at [date — to be completed].

---

## A note on the excerpts above

The criteria I have quoted are the portions of Aetna CPB 0736 — Hip Preservation Surgery available to me. The first criterion ends in a colon and introduces a list of conditions, and the policy contains further conditions that I have not reproduced here because I do not have their full text. I am not attempting to characterise any policy language beyond what I have quoted. Because the denial was issued for incomplete documentation rather than for a specific unmet criterion, I ask Aetna to identify in writing the exact criterion or criteria from this policy that it applied, and the specific document it found missing.

## What I am asking for

I ask Aetna to overturn the denial and authorize hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) as recommended by Dr. Reyes. In the alternative, I ask that Aetna tell me precisely which record is needed, so I can have it submitted promptly and have the request reviewed on a complete file. I would also like a copy of the clinical criteria used in this review.

I understand this appeal must be received by **January 28, 2027**, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am submitting it using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form, available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals, by fax to **859-425-3379** or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which I have confirmed before sending. Aetna can also be reached at 1-800-872-3862 or the number on my member card.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. Please contact me at the phone number or address above if anything further would help.

Sincerely,

**Reese Grant**
